questions.q: The keyboard shortcut to bookmark (favourite) the current page in all major browsers is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+D adds the current page to bookmarks/favourites. (Ctrl+B is bold in Office; in some browsers it toggles the bookmarks BAR, which is why the safe exam answer for bookmarking a page is Ctrl+D.)

questions.q: A hard copy of large engineering drawings is best produced on a:
questions.solution: Plotters draw precise, large-format line art (A0/A1 sheets) with a pen or cutting head - standard for CAD output. Printers handle page-size documents; a scanner is an input device.

questions.q: Which view prints one slide at the top with the speaker's notes below?
questions.solution: Notes Page view (and its print option) shows the slide above and its notes beneath - used while preparing to speak.
questions.shortcut: Slide on top, notes underneath = Notes Page.

questions.q: The national helpline number for reporting online financial fraud in India is:
questions.solution: 1930 is the cybercrime financial-fraud helpline (paired with the cybercrime.gov.in portal) for fast freezing of defrauded money. 181 is the women's helpline, 1098 childline, 100 police.

questions.q: According to the passage, why is night-time heat considered especially harmful?
options: Outdoor workers cannot complete their shifts at night
The body carries out its repair processes during sleep
Air conditioners stop working after sunset
Hospitals admit only night-time patients during heat waves
questions.solution: The passage states: 'Night-time heat is particularly dangerous because sleep is when the body repairs itself; hospitals report more admissions during hot nights...' — (b) restates the stated reason. (a) describes a para-2 problem about *day* shifts of workers, not nights. (c) is never said — the passage says the poor cannot afford electricity. (d) distorts the point about admissions being higher, not restricted, at night.
questions.shortcut: Anchor 'sleep' in para 2 and read the sentence — the answer is inside the 'because' clause.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Between you and I, / the newly appointed / manager has no / practical field experience.
questions.solution: A preposition takes object forms: *between you and **me***. *I* is a subject form and cannot follow *between*.
questions.shortcut: Preposition + I is always the error; flip it mentally: 'between me'.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is not capable ___ handling so much pressure at work.
questions.solution: The fixed collocation is **capable of** + V-ing. *capable for / in / to* are not standard.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

My elder brother is **two years senior** than me in service.
questions.solution: Latin comparatives (*senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior*) take **to**, never *than*: *two years senior to me*. 'More senior than' doubles the comparison; 'senior of' is not a form.
questions.shortcut: senior/junior/superior/inferior/prefer + to. Memorise the family of five.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.
2. The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha).
3. The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur was built by Rajendra I.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 ✔ — Kailasa (Cave 16), Ellora: **Krishna I** (Rashtrakuta).
2 ✔ — Shore Temple: **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)**.
3 ✘ — Brihadeeswara, Thanjavur: **Rajaraja I** (c. 1010). His son Rajendra I built the temple at **Gangaikondacholapuram**.
questions.shortcut: Statement 3 swaps father and son — once it is wrong, options C and D go; 1 is the well-known fact, so choose **1 and 2**.

questions.q: **National Sports Day** (29 August) is observed on the birth anniversary of —
questions.solution: Hockey wizard **Major Dhyan Chand** was born on 29 August 1905. The Khel Ratna is also named after him (since 2021).

questions.q: Gautama Buddha delivered his **first sermon** at —
questions.solution: The first sermon (*Dharmachakra-pravartana*, 'turning the wheel of law') was given at the Deer Park, **Sarnath**, near Varanasi. Birth – Lumbini; enlightenment – Bodh Gaya; death – Kushinagar.

questions.q: Which Sultan shifted his capital from Delhi to **Daulatabad (Devagiri)** in 1327?
questions.solution: **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** moved the capital to Daulatabad to control the Deccan, but soon had to return. He also issued the unsuccessful **token currency**.

questions.q: The average age of 30 students in a class is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average age increases by one year. The teacher's age is:
questions.solution: Teacher $= 31 \times 15 - 30 \times 14 = 465 - 420 = 45$ years.

questions.q: The simple interest on a certain sum at 5% per annum for 3 years is ₹900. The sum is:
questions.solution: $P = \frac{100 \times SI}{R \times T} = \frac{100 \times 900}{15} = 6000$, i.e. ₹6,000.

questions.shortcut: Recognise 0.027 = 0.3³, then answer = 2.3 − 0.3 = 2. Trap 2.6 is a + b.

questions.q: What is the sum of all prime numbers between 60 and 80?
questions.shortcut: Numbers ending in 1, 3, 7, 9 are the only candidates; strike out 63 (÷3), 69 (÷3), 77 (÷7).

questions.q:
**Statement:** Farmers in a district report that a new type of pest has been damaging their standing crops.

**Courses of action:**
I. The farmers should be told to stop cultivation in the district.
II. Agricultural experts should be sent to identify the pest and advise the farmers on control measures.

Which of the courses of action logically follow(s)?
options: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
questions.solution: I is drastic and destroys the farmers' livelihood instead of tackling the pest — **does not follow**. II is a practical step that addresses the actual problem — **follows**. Answer: **Only II**.
questions.shortcut: Tackle the pest, not the farming.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Precise, Preach, Predict, Precede, Precious.** Which word comes **fourth**?
questions.solution: All start PRE. 4th letter: A (Preach) < C (Precede, Precious, Precise) < D (Predict). Inside PREC: 5th letter E (Precede) < I (Precious, Precise); PRECI-O < PRECI-S. Order: Preach, Precede, Precious, Precise, Predict → fourth = **Precise**.
questions.shortcut: Peel the shared prefix one column at a time: PRE → A/C/D → E/I → O/S.

questions.q: All arrangements of the letters of **BEAD** are listed as in a dictionary. What is the **position of BEAD** in that list?
questions.solution: Sorted letters: A, B, D, E. B → 1 smaller (A) × 3! = 6. E → unused {A, D, E}: 2 smaller × 2! = 4. A → 0. D → 0. Rank = 6 + 4 + 0 + 0 + 1 = **11**.

questions.q: A square sheet is folded in half and then in half again, and **three** separate holes are punched through all the layers. How many holes will the unfolded sheet have?
questions.solution: Two full folds give 4 layers; each punch makes 4 holes: 3 × 4 = **12**.
